questions.prompt: What is the size (number of rows × columns) of [[2, 5, 1], [0, 3, 4]]?
questions.hint: Count the horizontal rows first, then count the entries across each row.
questions.solution: There are 2 rows, each with 3 entries, so the matrix is 2 × 3.
questions.aiConnection: A dataset can be stored as a matrix: rows might represent examples and columns might represent measured features.
questions.sourceTitle: Math is Fun · Introduction to Matrices

questions.hint: Add entries in matching positions, one position at a time.
questions.aiConnection: Adding matrices combines values stored in the same positions, such as contributions from two sources of data.

questions.hint: Scalar multiplication means multiplying each entry by the same number.
questions.aiConnection: Scaling a matrix changes the strength of every value together, similar to adjusting the scale of model weights.

questions.hint: For each result entry, multiply a row of the first matrix by a column of the second, then add.
questions.solution: Top-left: 1×2+2×1=4; top-right: 1×0+2×2=4; bottom row gives 10 and 8.
questions.aiConnection: Matrix multiplication is a core operation in neural networks: it combines inputs with learned weights.

questions.hint: Multiply each matrix row by the column vector and add the products.
questions.aiConnection: This is the simple shape of a neural-network layer: input values are combined with weights to make new values.

questions.hint: For a 2 × 2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]], calculate ad − bc.
questions.aiConnection: Determinants tell us whether a square matrix transformation preserves area or collapses a dimension.

questions.prompt: Which size matrix can be multiplied by a 2 × 3 matrix to produce a 2 × 2 result?
questions.hint: The inner dimensions must match; the outer dimensions become the result size.
questions.solution: (2 × 3)(3 × 2) is defined because the inner 3s match, and its result is 2 × 2.
questions.aiConnection: Matching matrix dimensions is like checking that a layer's output can fit the next layer's input.

questions.hint: The zero matrix has no effect when added to another matrix.
questions.solution: Adding zero to each corresponding entry leaves every original entry unchanged.
questions.aiConnection: The zero matrix is an additive identity, a useful reference point in equations and model updates.

questions.hint: Subtract entries in matching positions. Be careful when subtracting a negative number.
questions.aiConnection: A model can compare two matrices of values by subtracting them, for example to measure prediction error.

questions.prompt: What does multiplying a 2 × 2 identity matrix by [[7, 1], [0, 3]] do?
questions.hint: The identity matrix plays the same role for matrix multiplication that 1 plays for ordinary multiplication.
questions.solution: Multiplying by the identity matrix leaves the original matrix unchanged.
questions.aiConnection: Identity transformations are a useful baseline: a layer that applies identity weights passes its input through unchanged.
